summary:
Developed for NASA’s "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge, SoundSphere is an innovative browser-based web application that translates NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visual frames and multi-sensor satellite data into real-time harmonic soundscapes.
​Moving beyond traditional visual heatmaps that exclude over 253 million visually impaired individuals worldwide, SoundSphere implements rigorous psychoacoustic principles across over 1,000 tested hypotheses. It maps concurrent climate indicators—such as Sea Surface Temperature anomalies, NDVI vegetation, GEDI forest heights, atmospheric river moisture, and ISS lightning flash events—into non-masking polyphonic audio streams and percussive triggers.
​Powered by client-side procedural synthesis via Web Audio API and Tone.js, combined with 3D HRTF binaural spatialization and full WCAG 2.2 AAA screen-reader support, SoundSphere empowers blind researchers, students, and the public to "listen" to planetary dynamics and audibly pinpoint climate anomalies in real time.
details:
• What it does and how it works: SoundSphere is an innovative, browser-based web application designed for NASA's "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge. It operates by extracting individual visual frames and spatial data from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) content databases. The system dynamically translates these visual inputs—such as global carbon dioxide concentrations (DYAMOND Global Carbon Dioxide), canopy elevations (GEDI Forest Height), atmospheric moisture spread (3D View of an Atmospheric River), and rapid visual flashes (ISS Lightning Events 2017–2023)—into real-time, harmonic soundscapes and punctuated percussive triggers using the Web Audio API and Tone.js.
  • ​What benefits does it have? The project breaks down the traditional visual barrier of Earth science. By transforming complex, multidimensional planetary data into non-masking polyphonic audio streams and 3D spatial sound, it allows users to perceive environmental changes, thermal gradients, and atmospheric flows through hearing rather than relying solely on traditional visual GIS heatmaps.
  • ​What is the intended impact of the project? SoundSphere aims to democratize Earth science and achieve true STEM inclusion for over 253 million visually impaired and low-vision individuals worldwide. By integrating 3D binaural spatialization (HRTF) and full WCAG 2.2 AAA screen-reader compatibility, it empowers blind researchers, students, and museum visitors to independently explore NASA’s climate archives and detect ecological tipping points.
    • ​Languages & Core Tech: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+).
    • ​Audio Processing & Spatialization: Web Audio API, Tone.js, 3D PannerNode (HRTF).
    • ​NASA Visual Data & Resources: EIC Content Database, SVS visual sequences, DYAMOND Global Carbon Dioxide, GEDI Forest Height maps, 3D Atmospheric River models, ISS Lightning Events, and Global Sea Surface Currents/Temperature animations.
    • ​Deployment: GitHub Pages / Netlify.
  • ​How is your project creative? Rather than performing a naive pixel-to-sound translation that produces chaotic noise, SoundSphere applies rigorous artistic and scientific rulesets. It maps visual color spectrums, brightness, and spatial pixel density to precise musical parameters (pitch, rhythm, tempo, and timbre). For instance, it translates GEDI forest height color spectrums into rich harmonic overtones and maps ISS lightning flashes into instantaneous, punctuated percussive audio triggers.
  • ​What factors did your team consider? The team carefully balanced scientific fidelity with musical engagement by testing over 1,000 psychoacoustic hypotheses and implementing Albert Bregman’s Auditory Scene Analysis (ASA) framework. This ensured that multiple simultaneous data streams (such as carbon emissions, canopy density, and atmospheric moisture) remain distinct and non-masking. Additionally, the team prioritized universal accessibility, low-bandwidth browser execution (sub-25ms latency), and seamless user experience for both sighted and visually impaired users.
